description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Jaundice history structure
points: Painless vs painful onset, and the presence of pale stools with dark urine, are the fastest way to branch obstructive vs hepatocellular causes.
Always ask about alcohol use, known liver disease, and hepatotoxic medications.
Pruritus and pale stools point toward cholestasis / obstruction.

modules.title: Obstructive pattern
points: Painless jaundice with pale stools and dark urine suggests biliary obstruction — consider malignant obstruction in older patients (Courvoisier's law).
Fever plus RUQ pain plus jaundice (Charcot's triad) suggests ascending cholangitis — this is urgent.

Q000062.why_ask: Whether jaundice began with pain/fever or painlessly is the single most useful branching question.
Q000062.think: Painless progressive jaundice in an older patient raises malignant biliary obstruction on the differential.

Q000064.why_ask: Pale stool + dark urine together indicates conjugated (obstructive/cholestatic) hyperbilirubinaemia.
listen_for: Both present together vs isolated dark urine
Q000064.think: This combination should prioritise an obstructive work-up (ultrasound, LFTs pattern).

Q000063.why_ask: Alcohol use and known liver disease materially change the pre-test probability of hepatocellular causes.
Q000063.think: Document quantity and duration precisely — this affects both differential and counselling.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: painless jaundice branch
points: Consider malignant biliary obstruction, especially in older patients.
Check for a palpable non-tender gallbladder (Courvoisier's law) on exam.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: cholestatic pattern
points: Supports an obstructive/cholestatic process over pure haemolysis.
Prioritise abdominal ultrasound for biliary dilatation.
